# Brazil Potash AI-Powered X-Ray Transmission Sorting Testing Shows Potential for Higher Production and Longer Mine Life


October 13, 2026 6:45am EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_caf2ceb8e7935e8bd41f8ce22bebbb8a/brazilpotash/news/2026-10-13_Brazil_Potash_AI_Powered_X_Ray_Transmission_67.pdf)


- *AI-powered X-ray Transmission ("XRT") sorting testwork on samples of mineralized material successfully showed that approximately 20% of the tested lower-grade material could be screened out before reaching the processing plant, potentially freeing up capacity to increase production and/or extend mine life.*


- *Additional testwork, technical and economic studies will need to be done after commercial production to consider whether the technology could be incorporated into the Autazes Project.*


MANAUS, Brazil, Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Brazil Potash Corp. ("Brazil Potash" or the "Company") (NYSE American: GRO), a critical mineral exploration and development company advancing the Autazes Potash Project (the "Autazes Project" or "Project") in Amazonas State, Brazil, today announced positive initial results from its testing of Artificial Intelligence-powered X-ray Transmission (“XRT”) sorting technology, initiated when first announced in December 2025.


The testwork, conducted with engineering firm ERCOSPLAN, indicates that AI-powered XRT sorting technology is able to distinguish higher-grade potash mineralization from lower-grade material within the tested sample. The test was performed on ore greater than approximately 8 mm in size, and ERCOSPLAN anticipates that approximately 40% to 55% of the material it expects to mine will be greater than this size. In the initial test program, a sample containing approximately 13% KCl was upgraded to approximately 27% KCl, while the rejected fraction contained approximately 1% to 2% KCl. Based on the results obtained from the tested sample, approximately 20% of the lower-grade material in the sample was rejected prior to processing. Due to the small sample tested, the results are indicative and cannot yet be regarded as representative of full-scale mine production.


The Company intends to perform additional testwork and further engineering and economic analysis to consider and evaluate whether AI-powered XRT sorting technology could be implemented at the Autazes project to:


1. preconcentrate material and then hot leach process it to potentially increase production without the need to build a third mine shaft, and/or


2. access lower-grade areas of the Autazes potash deposit that are not economic to mine today, extending the mine’s operating life.


"These results show promise for Autazes," said Matt Simpson, CEO of Brazil Potash. "These initial results suggest that AI-powered XRT sorting technology can tell higher-grade potash mineralization apart from lower-grade material within the tested sample. This gives us an interesting opportunity to potentially unlock production flexibility down the road, whether that means a higher production rate and/or a longer mine life, subject to further testing and study. The next step is to test XRT sorting on a much larger sample after we initiate commercial production of the mine to potentially incorporate this technology."


The AI-powered XRT sorting system being tested is a third-party technology that incorporates data-driven classification tools to analyze individual particles and assess potential separation of higher-grade mineralized material from lower-grade material. The system supplier describes the technology as using deep learning and convolutional neural networks trained on millions of images to recognize complex features such as shape, size and colour, allowing it to distinguish materials that are difficult to separate with conventional sensors. The AI-analyzed data triggers high-speed valve blocks that fire precise bursts of air to eject lower-grade particles.


**Qualified Person**


The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Matt Simpson, Chief Executive Officer of the Company. Mr. Simpson is a Professional Engineer and a member of the Professional Engineers of Ontario. He is a Qualified Person as defined in National Instrument 43-101 – *Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects* ("NI 43-101").


**About Brazil Potash**


Brazil Potash (NYSE American: GRO) (www.brazilpotash.com), through its subsidiary Potássio do Brasil, is developing the Autazes Project to supply potash to one of the world's largest agricultural exporters. Brazil is critical for global food security, with among the highest amounts of fresh water and arable land and an ideal climate for year-round crop growth, yet the country imported approximately 96% of the potash it consumed in 2025 despite hosting what is anticipated to be one of the world's largest undeveloped potash basins. The potash produced will be transported primarily using low-cost river barges on an inland river system in partnership with Amaggi (www.amaggi.com.br), one of Brazil's largest farmers and logistical operators of agricultural products.
